title.zh: 卷六十七 吳越世家第七: 錢鏐
title.raw: 卷六十七 吳越世家第七: 錢鏐 Volume 67: Hereditary House of Wuyue

sentences.zh: 錢镠，字具美，杭州臨安人也。

translations.literal: Qian Liu, styled Jumei, was a native of Lin'an in Hangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Liu, whose style name was Jumei, came from Lin'an in Hangzhou.

sentences.zh: 臨安里中有大木，镠幼時與群兒戲木下，镠坐大石指麾群兒為隊伍，號令頗有法，群兒皆憚之。

translations.literal: In his village in Lin'an there was a great tree; when Liu was young he played with other boys beneath it, sitting on a large stone and directing them into ranks; his orders were quite orderly, and all the boys feared him.
translations.idiomatic: A great tree stood in his neighborhood in Lin'an. As a boy Liu played beneath it, seated on a large stone while he drilled the other children into formation; his commands were surprisingly disciplined, and the boys all stood in awe of him.

sentences.zh: 及壯，無賴，不喜事生業，以販鹽為盜。

translations.literal: When he grew up he was a ruffian, took no interest in honest livelihood, and made a living smuggling salt as a bandit.
translations.idiomatic: When he came of age he was a wastrel who shunned honest work and lived by smuggling salt and raiding as a outlaw.

sentences.zh: 縣錄事鐘起有子數人，與镠飲博，起嘗禁其諸子，諸子多竊從之遊。

translations.literal: The county registrar Zhong Qi had several sons who drank and gambled with Liu; Qi once forbade his sons, but they often stole away to keep company with him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhong Qi, the county registrar, had several sons who drank and gambled with Liu. Qi tried to keep his sons away, but they often slipped off to join Liu anyway.

sentences.zh: 豫章人有善術者，望牛鬥間有王氣。

translations.literal: A man of Yuzhang skilled in occult arts gazed at the region between the Ox and Dipper constellations and saw a kingly aura.
translations.idiomatic: A practitioner of divination from Yuzhang observed the Ox and Dipper asterisms and discerned an aura of kingship there.

sentences.zh: 牛鬥，錢塘分也，因遊錢塘。

translations.literal: The Ox and Dipper lay in the Qiantang region, so he traveled to Qiantang.
translations.idiomatic: Since those constellations corresponded to the Qiantang area, he went there to investigate.

sentences.zh: 占之在臨安，乃之臨安，以相法隱市中，陰求其人。

translations.literal: His divination placed the man in Lin'an; he went to Lin'an, concealed himself in the market practicing physiognomy, and secretly sought the person.
translations.idiomatic: His readings pointed to Lin'an, so he went there, set up as a face-reader in the marketplace, and quietly searched for the man of destiny.

sentences.zh: 起與術者善，術者私謂起曰：「占君縣有貴人，求之市中不可得，視君之相貴矣，然不足當之。

translations.literal: Qi was on good terms with the adept, who privately told Qi, "Your county has a noble man; I cannot find him in the market. By your features you are noble, yet not noble enough to match it."
translations.idiomatic: Qi knew the diviner well. The man took Qi aside and said, "My readings say a man of great rank is in your county, but I cannot find him in the markets. You yourself look distinguished, yet you are not the one the stars foretell."

sentences.zh: 」起乃為置酒，悉召賢豪為會，陰令術者遍視之，皆不足當。

translations.literal: Qi then set out wine, summoned all the local worthies to a gathering, and secretly had the adept examine them one by one; none measured up.
translations.idiomatic: Qi hosted a feast and invited every leading man in the district, while the diviner studied each guest in secret. None of them matched the omen.

sentences.zh: 術者過起家，镠適從外來，見起，反走，術者望見之，大驚曰：「此真貴人也！

translations.literal: The adept passed Qi's house just as Liu was coming in from outside; seeing Qi he turned to flee. The adept caught sight of him and cried in alarm, "This is the true noble!"
translations.idiomatic: The diviner happened to pass Qi's home as Liu was returning from outside. Liu saw Qi and ran the other way, but the diviner glimpsed him and exclaimed in shock, "There is the man of destiny!"

sentences.zh: 」起笑曰：「此吾旁舍錢生爾。

translations.literal: Qi laughed and said, "That is only young Qian from next door."
translations.idiomatic: Qi laughed. "That is just the Qian boy from next door."

sentences.zh: 」術者召镠至，熟視之，顧起曰：「君之貴者，因此人也。

translations.literal: The adept summoned Liu, studied him closely, and turning to Qi said, "The nobility destined for you comes through this man."
translations.idiomatic: The diviner called Liu over, studied his face at length, then told Qi, "Whatever greatness awaits you will come through this youth."

sentences.zh: 」乃慰镠曰：「子骨法非常，願自愛。

translations.literal: He then comforted Liu, saying, "Your bone structure is extraordinary; take good care of yourself."
translations.idiomatic: He urged Liu gently, "Your features are unlike any I have seen. Guard yourself well."

sentences.zh: 」因與起訣曰：「吾求其人者，非有所欲也，直欲質吾術爾。

translations.literal: He then took leave of Qi, saying, "In seeking this man I wanted nothing for myself; I only wished to test my art."
translations.idiomatic: Bidding Qi farewell, he added, "I sought him with no ulterior motive—only to prove whether my craft was true."

sentences.zh: 」明日乃去。

translations.literal: The next day he departed.
translations.idiomatic: He left the following day.

sentences.zh: 起始縱其子等與镠遊，時時貸其窮乏。

translations.literal: At the start, Qi allowed his sons and others to go about with Qian Liu, and from time to time lent him relief when he was poor and in want.
translations.idiomatic: In his early years, Qi let his sons and others go out with Qian Liu, and from time to time helped him out when he was short of means.

sentences.zh: 镠善射與槊，稍通圖緯諸書。

translations.literal: Qian Liu was skilled at archery and the spear, and gradually came to understand books on charts of the cosmos, prophecies, and the like.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Liu was skilled with bow and spear, and gradually gained some knowledge of astrology, omens, and related texts.

sentences.zh: 唐乾符二年，浙西裨將王郢作亂，石鑒鎮將董昌募鄉兵討賊，表镠偏將，擊郢破之。

translations.literal: In the second year of Qianfu of Tang, the Zhexi deputy general Wang Ying rose in rebellion; the Shijian garrison commander Dong Chang recruited local militia to attack the bandits, recommended Qian Liu as a deputy commander, struck Wang Ying, and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of the Qianfu era (875), Wang Ying, a deputy general in Zhexi, rose in rebellion. Dong Chang, military commissioner at Shijian, recruited local militia to suppress the rebels, had Qian Liu appointed deputy commander, attacked Wang Ying, and defeated him.

sentences.zh: 是時，黃巢眾已數千，攻掠浙東，至臨安，镠曰：「今鎮兵少而賊兵多，難以力禦，宜出奇兵邀之。

translations.literal: At this time Huang Chao's followers already numbered several thousand; they raided eastern Zhejiang and reached Lin'an. Qian Liu said, "Now the garrison troops are few while the bandit troops are many—it is hard to resist them by force; we should use surprise troops to intercept them.
translations.idiomatic: By then Huang Chao's followers already numbered in the thousands. They raided eastern Zhejiang and reached Lin'an. Qian Liu said, "Our garrison is too small to meet their numbers head-on. We should lay an ambush with a strike force."

sentences.zh: 」乃與勁卒二十人伏山谷中，巢先鋒度險皆單騎，镠伏弩射殺其將，巢兵亂，镠引勁卒蹂之，斬首數百級。

translations.literal: Thereupon, with twenty picked soldiers he hid in a mountain valley; Huang Chao's vanguard, crossing difficult terrain, all rode alone. Qian Liu, lying in wait with crossbows, shot and killed their commander; Huang Chao's soldiers fell into disorder, and Qian Liu led his picked soldiers to trample them, severing heads by the hundreds.
translations.idiomatic: He took twenty picked men and hid in a mountain valley. Huang Chao's vanguard, traversing the difficult pass, rode singly. Qian Liu's ambush crossbows killed their leader; the rebels broke ranks, and he charged with his picked men, cutting down hundreds.

sentences.zh: 镠曰：「此可一用爾，大眾至何可敵邪！

translations.literal: Qian Liu said, "This trick can be used once—that is all; when the main force arrives, how could we oppose them!"
translations.idiomatic: Qian Liu said, "That ruse works once—no more. When their main body arrives, we cannot stand against them."

sentences.zh: 」乃引兵趨八百里，八百里，地名也，告道旁媼曰：「後有問者，告曰：『臨安兵屯八百里矣。

translations.literal: Thereupon he led his troops to hasten to Baibaili—Baibaili was a place name—and told an old woman by the road, "When people ask later, tell them, 'The Lin'an troops are encamped at Baibaili.'"
translations.idiomatic: He marched his men to a place called Baibaili (Eight Hundred Li). He told an old woman by the roadside, "If anyone asks later, say, 'The Lin'an troops are stationed at Baibaili.'"

sentences.zh: 』」巢眾至，聞媼語，不知其地名，曰：「向十餘卒不可敵，況八百里乎！

translations.literal: Huang Chao's masses arrived, heard the old woman's words, did not know it was a place name, and said, "Just now a dozen-odd soldiers could not be withstood—how much less eight hundred li!"
translations.idiomatic: When Huang Chao's forces arrived and heard the old woman's words, not knowing Baibaili was a place name, they said, "We could barely handle a dozen men just now—how could we face eight hundred li of them!"

sentences.zh: 」遂急引兵過。

translations.literal: Thereupon they hurriedly led their troops away past it.
translations.idiomatic: So they hurried on past without stopping.

sentences.zh: 都統高駢聞巢不敢犯臨安，壯之，召董昌與镠俱至廣陵。

translations.literal: The overall commander Gao Piao heard that Huang Chao did not dare to invade Lin'an, admired this, and summoned Dong Chang and Qian Liu together to Guangling.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Piao, the overall commander, heard that Huang Chao had not dared to attack Lin'an and was impressed. He summoned Dong Chang and Qian Liu to Guangling together.

sentences.zh: 久之，駢無討賊意，昌等不見用，辭還，駢表昌杭州刺史。

translations.literal: After a long while, Piao had no intention of attacking the bandits; Chang and the others were not employed, took leave and returned; Piao memorialized to appoint Chang as prefect of Hangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In time Gao Piao showed no interest in suppressing the rebels, and Dong Chang and his men were given no role. They asked to leave and returned home; Gao Piao recommended Dong Chang for the post of prefect of Hangzhou.

sentences.zh: 是時，天下已亂，昌乃團諸縣兵為八都，以镠為都指揮使，成及為靖江都將。

translations.literal: At this time the empire was already in disorder; Chang thereupon organized the troops of the various counties into eight commands, appointing Qian Liu as commander of the commands and Cheng Ji as commander of the Jingjiang command.
translations.idiomatic: With the empire already in turmoil, Dong Chang organized county militia into eight commands, made Qian Liu overall commander, and Cheng Ji commander of the Jingjiang command.

sentences.zh: 中和二年，越州觀察使劉漢宏與昌有隙，漢宏遣其弟漢宥、都虞候辛約，屯兵西陵。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhonghe, Liu Hanhong, governor of Yuezhou, had a rift with Chang; Hanhong sent his younger brother Hanyou and chief adjutant Xin Yue to encamp troops at Xiling.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of the Zhonghe era (882), Liu Hanhong, military governor of Yue prefecture, fell out with Dong Chang. Hanhong sent his brother Hanyou and chief adjutant Xin Yue to station troops at Xiling.

sentences.zh: 镠率八都兵渡江，竊取軍號，斫其營，營中驚擾，因焚之，漢宥等皆走。

translations.literal: Qian Liu led the troops of the eight commands across the river, secretly took their military signals, struck their camp; the camp was alarmed and thrown into turmoil, and he thereupon burned it; Hanyou and the others all fled.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Liu crossed the river with the eight commands, seized their camp signals in stealth, and raided their camp. Panic spread through the encampment; he burned it, and Hanyou and the rest fled.

sentences.zh: 漢宏復遣將黃珪、何肅屯諸暨、蕭山，镠皆攻破之。

translations.literal: Hanhong again sent the generals Huang Gui and He Su to encamp at Zhuji and Xiaoshan; Qian Liu attacked and broke them all.
translations.idiomatic: Hanhong sent Huang Gui and He Su to garrison Zhuji and Xiaoshan; Qian Liu defeated them both.

sentences.zh: 與漢宏遇，戰，大敗之，殺何肅、辛約。

translations.literal: He encountered Hanhong, fought, and greatly defeated him, killing He Su and Xin Yue.
translations.idiomatic: He met Liu Hanhong in battle, routed him, and killed He Su and Xin Yue.

sentences.zh: 漢宏易服持膾刀以遁，追者及之，漢宏曰：「我宰夫也。

translations.literal: Hanhong changed clothes, took a carving knife for slicing meat, and fled; pursuers caught up with him, and Hanhong said, "I am a butcher."
translations.idiomatic: Liu Hanhong disguised himself and fled with a butcher's cleaver in hand. When pursuers caught up, he said, "I'm just a butcher."

sentences.zh: 」舉刀示之，乃免。

translations.literal: He raised the knife to show them, and was thus spared.
translations.idiomatic: He held up the knife to prove it, and they let him go.

sentences.zh: 四年，僖宗遣中使焦居璠為杭、越通和使，詔昌及漢宏罷兵，皆不奉詔。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, Emperor Xizong sent the eunuch envoy Jiao Jufan as peace envoy for Hang and Yue, ordering Chang and Hanhong to cease hostilities; neither obeyed the edict.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Zhonghe (884), Emperor Xizong sent the eunuch Jiao Jufan as peace commissioner between Hang and Yue, ordering Dong Chang and Liu Hanhong to stand down. Neither complied.

sentences.zh: 漢宏遣其將朱褒、韓公玫、施堅實等以舟兵屯望海。

translations.literal: Hanhong sent his generals Zhu Bao, Han Gongmei, Shi Jianshi, and others with river troops to encamp at Wanghai.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Hanhong sent Zhu Bao, Han Gongmei, Shi Jianshi, and others with naval forces to station at Wanghai.

sentences.zh: 镠出平水，成及夜率奇兵破褒等於曹娥埭，進屯豐山，施堅實等降，遂攻破越州。

translations.literal: Qian Liu advanced from Pingshui; Cheng Ji by night led surprise troops and defeated Bao and the others at Cao'e Dam, advanced and encamped at Fengshan; Shi Jianshi and the others surrendered, and he thereupon attacked and took Yuezhou.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Liu moved from Pingshui. Cheng Ji led a night raid at Cao'e Dam and routed Zhu Bao's force, then advanced to Fengshan. Shi Jianshi and others surrendered, and they took Yuezhou.

sentences.zh: 漢宏走臺州，臺州刺史執漢宏送於镠，斬於會稽，族其家。

translations.literal: Hanhong fled to Taizhou; the prefect of Taizhou seized Hanhong and delivered him to Qian Liu; he was executed at Kuaiji, and his clan was exterminated.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Hanhong fled to Taizhou. The prefect there seized him and delivered him to Qian Liu, who executed him at Kuaiji and wiped out his family.

sentences.zh: 镠乃奏昌代漢寵，而自居杭州。

translations.literal: Qian Liu thereupon memorialized that Chang should replace Liu Hanhong, while he himself took up residence at Hangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Liu then recommended Dong Chang to replace Liu Hanhong, while he himself established his base at Hangzhou.

sentences.zh: 光啟三年，拜镠左衛大將軍、杭州刺史，昌越州觀察使。

translations.literal: In the third year of Guangqi, Qian Liu was appointed Left Guard Grand General and prefect of Hangzhou; Chang was made governor of Yuezhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of the Guangqi era (887), Qian Liu was appointed Left Guard Grand General and prefect of Hangzhou; Dong Chang became military governor of Yue prefecture.

sentences.zh: 是歲，畢師鐸囚高駢，淮南大亂，六合鎮將徐約攻取蘇州。

translations.literal: That year, Bi Shiduo imprisoned Gao Piao; Huainan was greatly in disorder; the Liuhe garrison commander Xu Yue attacked and took Suzhou.
translations.idiomatic: That year Bi Shiduo imprisoned Gao Piao, throwing Huainan into chaos. Xu Yue, military commissioner at Liuhe, captured Suzhou.

sentences.zh: 潤州牙將劉浩逐其帥周寶，寶奔常州，浩推度支催勘官薛朗為帥。

translations.literal: Liu Hao, an officer of the Runzhou guard corps, drove out his commander Zhou Bao; Bao fled to Changzhou; Hao promoted the revenue audit official Xue Lang as commander.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Hao, a guard officer at Run prefecture, deposed his commander Zhou Bao, who fled to Changzhou. Liu Hao installed Xue Lang, a revenue audit official, as the new commander.

sentences.zh: 镠遣都將成及、杜棱等攻常州，取周寶以歸，镠具軍禮郊迎，館寶於樟亭，寶病卒。

translations.literal: Qian Liu sent the commanders Cheng Ji, Du Ling, and others to attack Changzhou, took Zhou Bao and brought him back; Qian Liu prepared full military rites to welcome him at the suburbs, lodged Bao at Zhangting; Bao died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Liu sent Cheng Ji, Du Ling, and others to attack Changzhou and bring Zhou Bao back. Qian Liu welcomed him at the city outskirts with full military honors and housed him at Zhang Pavilion, where Zhou Bao died of illness.

sentences.zh: 棱等進攻潤州，逐劉浩，執薛朗，剖其心以祭寶。

translations.literal: Ling and the others advanced to attack Runzhou, drove out Liu Hao, seized Xue Lang, cut open his heart to offer sacrifice to Bao.
translations.idiomatic: Du Ling and his men then attacked Runzhou, expelled Liu Hao, captured Xue Lang, and cut out his heart as an offering to Zhou Bao's spirit.

sentences.zh: 然後遣其弟钅求攻徐約，約敗走入海，追殺之。

translations.literal: Thereafter he sent his younger brother Qian Qiu to attack Xu Yue; Yue was defeated and fled into the sea; they pursued and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: He then sent his younger brother Qian Qiu against Xu Yue. Xu Yue was defeated, fled into the sea, and was pursued and killed.

sentences.zh: 昭宗拜镠杭州防禦使。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhaozong appointed Qian Liu defensive commissioner of Hangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhaozong appointed Qian Liu defensive commissioner of Hangzhou.

sentences.zh: 是時，楊行密、孫儒爭淮南，與镠戰蘇、常間。

translations.literal: At this time Yang Xingmi and Sun Ru contested Huainan; they fought Qian Liu between Suzhou and Changzhou.
translations.idiomatic: At this time Yang Xingmi and Sun Ru were fighting over Huainan and clashed with Qian Liu in the Suzhou–Changzhou region.

sentences.zh: 久之，儒為行密所殺，行密據淮南，取潤州，镠亦取蘇、常。

translations.literal: After a long while, Ru was killed by Xingmi; Xingmi held Huainan and took Runzhou; Qian Liu also took Suzhou and Changzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In time Sun Ru was killed by Yang Xingmi. Yang Xingmi secured Huainan and took Runzhou; Qian Liu recovered Suzhou and Changzhou.

sentences.zh: 唐升越州威勝軍，以董昌為節度使，封隴西郡王；

translations.literal: Tang promoted Yuezhou to the Weisheng Army, making Dong Chang its military governor and enfeoffing him as Prince of Longxi Commandery;
translations.idiomatic: The Tang court elevated Yue prefecture to the Weisheng Army, appointed Dong Chang its military governor, and enfeoffed him as Prince of Longxi;

sentences.zh: 杭州武勝軍，拜镠都團練使，以成及為副使。

translations.literal: Hangzhou was made the Wusheng Army; Qian Liu was appointed military training commissioner, with Cheng Ji as deputy commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Hangzhou became the Wusheng Army; Qian Liu was named overall military training commissioner, with Cheng Ji as his deputy.

sentences.zh: 及字弘濟，與镠同事攻討，謀多出於及，而镠以女妻及子仁琇。

translations.literal: Ji, courtesy name Hongji, together with Qian Liu carried out joint attacks and suppressions; many plans issued from Ji, and Qian Liu gave his daughter in marriage to Ji's son Renxiu.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Ji, courtesy name Hongji, fought alongside Qian Liu in many campaigns; much of the strategy came from Cheng Ji, and Qian Liu gave his daughter in marriage to Cheng Ji's son Renxiu.

sentences.zh: 镠乃以杜棱、阮結、顧全武等為將校，沈崧、皮光業、林鼎、羅隱為賓客。

translations.literal: Liu thereupon made Du Ling, Ruan Jie, Gu Quanwu, and others his officers, and Shen Song, Pi Guangye, Lin Ding, and Luo Yin his retainers.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Liu then appointed Du Ling, Ruan Jie, and Gu Quanwu among others as his commanders, and Shen Song, Pi Guangye, Lin Ding, and Luo Yin as his advisers.

sentences.zh: 景福二年，拜镠鎮海軍節度使、潤州刺史。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jingfu, Liu was appointed Military Commissioner of the Zhenhai Army and Prefect of Runzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Jingfu, Qian Liu was appointed Military Commissioner of the Zhenhai Army and Prefect of Runzhou.

sentences.zh: 乾寧元年，加同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qianning, he was given the additional title of Grand Councilor of the Secretariat-Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Qianning, he was made a Grand Councilor of the Secretariat-Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 二年，越州董昌反。

translations.literal: In the second year, Dong Chang of Yuezhou rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year, Dong Chang rebelled at Yuezhou.

sentences.zh: 昌素愚，不能決事，臨民訟，以骰子擲之，而勝者為直。

translations.literal: Chang was by nature foolish and could not decide affairs; when facing the people's lawsuits, he would cast dice, and whichever side won was deemed in the right.
translations.idiomatic: Chang was naturally dim-witted and incapable of judgment. When common folk brought lawsuits before him, he would toss dice—and whichever side won he declared right.

sentences.zh: 妖人應智王溫、巫韓媼等，以妖言惑昌，獻鳥獸為符瑞。

translations.literal: Sorcerers Ying Zhi and Wang Wen, the witch Han Ao, and others used occult speech to delude Chang, presenting birds and beasts as signs of heavenly favor.
translations.idiomatic: Sorcerers such as Ying Zhi and Wang Wen, and the witch Han Ao, beguiled Chang with occult talk and offered up birds and beasts as portents of imperial destiny.

sentences.zh: 牙將倪德儒謂昌曰：「曩時謠言有羅平鳥主越人禍福，民間多圖其形禱祠之，視王書名與圖類。

translations.literal: Guard officer Ni Deru said to Chang: "Formerly a rumor held that there was a Luoping Bird that ruled the fortune and misfortune of the people of Yue; among the folk many drew its form and prayed to it—the King's written name resembles the image in the drawing.
translations.idiomatic: Guard officer Ni Deru said to Chang: "There was once a prophecy about a Luoping Bird that governed the fate of the people of Yue. Country folk widely copied its likeness and set up altars to it—and Your Majesty's written name looks just like that bird in the pictures.

sentences.zh: 」因出圖以示昌。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he produced the picture to show Chang.
translations.idiomatic: " With that he brought out the picture and showed it to Chang.

sentences.zh: 昌大悅，乃自稱皇帝，國號羅平，改元順天。

translations.literal: Chang was greatly pleased, and thereupon styled himself Emperor, with the state name Luoping and reign title Shuntian.
translations.idiomatic: Chang was overjoyed. He declared himself emperor, named his realm Luoping, and adopted the reign title Shuntian.

sentences.zh: 分其兵為兩軍，中軍衣黃，外軍衣白，銘其衣曰「歸義」。

translations.literal: He divided his troops into two armies: the central army wore yellow, the outer army white, and on their garments was inscribed "Returning to Righteousness."
translations.idiomatic: He split his forces into two armies—the center corps in yellow, the outer corps in white—with the words "Returning to Righteousness" emblazoned on their uniforms.

sentences.zh: 副使黃竭切戒昌以為不可，昌大怒，使人斬竭，持其首至，罵曰：「此賊負我好聖，明時三公不肯作，乃自求死邪！

translations.literal: Vice Commissioner Huang Jie urgently admonished Chang that this could not be done; Chang was greatly enraged, had men behead Jie, brought his head forward, and cursed: "This traitor failed my kindness and sagehood—given a bright age he would not accept the rank of Three Excellencies, yet sought death of his own accord!
translations.idiomatic: Vice Commissioner Huang Jie urgently warned Chang that he must not do this. Chang flew into a rage, had Jie executed, and when the severed head was brought before him he cursed it: "This villain spurned my favor in an enlightened age! The rank of the Three Excellencies was his for the taking—yet he chose to throw his life away!

sentences.zh: 」投之圊中。

translations.literal: " He cast it into the latrine.
translations.idiomatic: " He tossed the head into a privy pit.

sentences.zh: 昌乃以書告镠，镠以昌反狀聞。

translations.literal: Chang then sent a letter to inform Liu; Liu reported Chang's rebellious conduct to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Chang then wrote to inform Liu, and Liu reported Dong Chang's rebellion to the court.

sentences.zh: 昭宗下詔削昌官爵，封镠彭城郡王，浙江東道招討使。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhaozong issued an edict stripping Chang of rank and titles, enfeoffing Liu as Prince of Pengcheng and Pacification Commissioner of Zhejiang East Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhaozong stripped Chang of his titles by edict, enfeoffed Qian Liu as Prince of Pengcheng, and appointed him Pacification Commissioner for Zhejiang East.

sentences.zh: 镠曰：「董氏於吾有恩，不可遽伐。

translations.literal: Liu said: "The Dong clan once showed me kindness; I cannot hastily attack them.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Liu said: "The Dong family once did me a kindness. I cannot attack them rashly.

sentences.zh: 」以兵三萬屯迎恩門，遣其客沈滂諭昌使改過。

translations.literal: " He encamped thirty thousand troops at Ying'en Gate and sent his client Shen Pang to instruct Chang to reform his conduct.
translations.idiomatic: " He posted thirty thousand men at the Ying'en Gate and sent his retainer Shen Pang to urge Chang to repent and mend his ways.

sentences.zh: 昌以錢二百萬犒軍，執應智等送軍中，自請待罪，镠乃還兵。

translations.literal: Chang gave two million in cash to reward the army, seized Ying Zhi and the others and sent them to the camp, himself requesting to await punishment, and Liu then withdrew his troops.
translations.idiomatic: Chang sent two million strings of cash to reward Liu's army, handed over Ying Zhi and his confederates, and submitted himself to judgment. Liu thereupon withdrew his forces.

sentences.zh: 昌復拒命，遣其將陳郁、崔溫等屯香嚴、石侯，乞兵於楊行密，行密遣安仁義救昌。

translations.literal: Chang again defied orders, sent his generals Chen Yu, Cui Wen, and others to encamp at Xiangyan and Shihou, begged troops from Yang Xingmi, and Xingmi dispatched An Renyi to rescue Chang.
translations.idiomatic: Chang defied orders once more. He posted his generals Chen Yu and Cui Wen at Xiangyan and Shihou, appealed to Yang Xingmi for reinforcements, and Xingmi sent An Renyi to Chang's aid.

sentences.zh: 镠遣顧全武攻昌，斬崔溫。

translations.literal: Liu dispatched Gu Quanwu to attack Chang and beheaded Cui Wen.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Liu sent Gu Quanwu against Chang and had Cui Wen killed.

sentences.zh: 昌所用諸將徐珣、湯臼、袁邠皆庸人，不知兵，遇全武輒敗。

translations.literal: The various generals Chang employed—Xu Xun, Tang Jiu, and Yuan Bin—were all mediocre men who knew nothing of warfare; whenever they met Quanwu they were defeated.
translations.idiomatic: The commanders Chang relied on—Xu Xun, Tang Jiu, and Yuan Bin—were mediocre men with no grasp of war. Whenever they faced Quanwu they were routed.

sentences.zh: 昌兄子真，驍勇善戰，全武等攻之，逾年不能克。

translations.literal: Chang's elder brother's son Zhen was fierce and brave, skilled in battle; Quanwu and the others attacked him for more than a year without prevailing.
translations.idiomatic: Chang's nephew Zhen was bold and skilled in battle. Quanwu and his colleagues besieged him for more than a year without success.

sentences.zh: 真與其裨將刺羽有隙，羽譖之，昌殺真，兵乃敗。

translations.literal: Zhen had a rift with his lieutenant Ci Yu; Yu slandered him, Chang killed Zhen, and the army then collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen had fallen out with his lieutenant Ci Yu. Yu denounced him, Chang had Zhen executed, and the army's defeat followed.

sentences.zh: 全武執昌歸杭州，行至西小江，昌顧左右曰：「吾與錢公俱起鄉里，吾嘗為大將，今何面復見之乎！

translations.literal: Quanwu seized Chang and returned to Hangzhou; when they reached West Xiao River, Chang looked to those at his side and said: "Lord Qian and I both rose from the same countryside; I was once a great general—what face have I now to see him again!
translations.idiomatic: Quanwu captured Chang and marched him back to Hangzhou. At West Xiao River, Chang turned to his attendants and said: "Lord Qian and I came up from the same countryside together. I was once a great commander—what shame could I bear to show my face before him now?

sentences.zh: 」左右相對泣下，因瞋目大呼，投水死。

translations.literal: " Those at his side wept facing one another; then he glared, gave a great shout, and cast himself into the water to die.
translations.idiomatic: " His attendants wept helplessly. Then he glared, cried out, and drowned himself in the river.

sentences.zh: 昭宗以宰相王溥鎮越州，溥請授镠，乃改威勝軍為鎮東軍，拜镠鎮海、鎮東軍節度使、加檢校太尉、中書令，賜鐵券，恕九死。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhaozong sent Grand Councilor Wang Pu to govern Yuezhou; Pu requested that it be granted to Liu, whereupon Weisheng Army was changed to Zhendong Army, Liu was appointed Military Commissioner of Zhenhai and Zhendong, given the additional posts of Acting Grand Guardian and Director of the Secretariat, and granted an iron tally forgiving nine deaths.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhaozong had Grand Councilor Wang Pu take charge of Yuezhou. Pu petitioned that the territory be transferred to Liu, and the Weisheng command was redesignated Zhendong. Qian Liu was made Military Commissioner of both Zhenhai and Zhendong, elevated to Acting Grand Guardian and Director of the Secretariat, and granted an iron tally forgiving nine capital crimes.

sentences.zh: 镠如越州受命，還治錢塘，號越州為「東府」。

translations.literal: Liu went to Yuezhou to receive his commission, returned to govern Qiantang, and styled Yuezhou the "Eastern Capital."
translations.idiomatic: Qian Liu went to Yuezhou to accept his appointment, returned to rule from Qiantang, and styled Yuezhou his "Eastern Capital."

sentences.zh: 光化元年，移鎮海軍於杭州，加镠檢校太師，改镠鄉里曰廣義鄉勛貴裏，镠素所居營曰衣錦營。

translations.literal: In the first year of Guanghua, the Zhenhai Army was moved to Hangzhou; Liu was given the additional title Acting Grand Preceptor; Liu's native village was renamed Guangyi Township, Xungui Lane; and the camp where he had long resided was called the Brocade-Robed Camp.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Guanghua the Zhenhai command was shifted to Hangzhou. Qian Liu was promoted to Acting Grand Preceptor. His home village was renamed Guangyi Township, Lane of Meritorious Nobility, and the camp where he had long lived was called the Brocade-Robed Camp.

sentences.zh: 婺州刺史王壇叛附於淮南，楊行密遣其將康儒應壇，因攻睦州。

translations.literal: Wang Tan, Prefect of Wuzhou, rebelled and submitted to Huainan; Yang Xingmi sent his general Kang Ru to support Tan, and thereby attacked Muzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Tan, Prefect of Wuzhou, rebelled and went over to Huainan. Yang Xingmi sent his general Kang Ru to join him, and together they attacked Muzhou.

sentences.zh: 镠遣其弟钅求敗儒於軒渚，壇奔宣州。

translations.literal: Liu sent his younger brother Qiu to defeat Ru at Xuanzhu, and Tan fled to Xuanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Liu sent his younger brother Qian Qiu to defeat Kang Ru at Xuanzhu. Wang Tan fled to Xuanzhou.

sentences.zh: 昭宗詔镠圖形淩煙閣，升衣錦營為衣錦城，石鑒山曰衣錦山，大官山曰功臣山。

translations.literal: Emperor Zhaozong ordered that Liu's portrait be placed in Lingyan Pavilion; the Brocade-Robed Camp was elevated to Brocade-Robed City; Stone Mirror Mountain was renamed Brocade-Robed Mountain; and Great Official Mountain was renamed Mountain of Meritorious Ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Zhaozong commanded that Qian Liu's likeness be enshrined in the Lingyan Pavilion. The Brocade-Robed Camp was elevated to Brocade-Robed City, Stone Mirror Mountain became Brocade-Robed Mountain, and Great Official Mountain was renamed Mountain of Meritorious Ministers.

sentences.zh: 镠遊衣錦城，宴故老，山林皆覆以錦，號其幼所嘗戲大木曰「衣錦將軍」。

translations.literal: Liu toured Brocade-Robed City, feasted the elders of old acquaintance, draped the hills and forests all in brocade, and styled the great tree beneath which he had played as a child the "Brocade-Robed General."
translations.idiomatic: Qian Liu toured Brocade-Robed City and held a feast for the village elders. He had the hills and woods draped in brocade, and named the great tree under which he had played as a boy the "Brocade-Robed General."

sentences.zh: 天復二年，封镠越王。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianfu, Liu was enfeoffed as King of Yue.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Tianfu, Qian Liu was enfeoffed as King of Yue.

sentences.zh: 镠巡衣錦城，武勇右都指揮使徐綰與左都指揮使許再思叛，焚掠城郭，攻內城，镠子傳瑛及其將馬綽、陳為等閉門拒之。

translations.literal: While Liu was inspecting Brocade-Robed City, Right Commandant of Martial Valor Xu Kuo and Left Commandant Xu Zaisi rebelled, burned and plundered the city walls, attacked the inner city, and Liu's son Chuanying together with his generals Ma Chuo, Chen Wei, and others shut the gates to resist them.
translations.idiomatic: While Qian Liu was touring Brocade-Robed City, Xu Kuo, Right Commandant of Martial Valour, and Xu Zaisi, Left Commandant, rose in revolt. They burned and looted the outer city and assaulted the inner citadel. Liu's son Chuanying, with the generals Ma Chuo and Chen Wei among others, barred the gates and held them off.

sentences.zh: 镠歸，至北郭門不得入。

translations.literal: Liu returned, reached the North Suburban Gate, and could not enter.
translations.idiomatic: When Qian Liu returned he found himself shut out at the North Suburban Gate.

sentences.zh: 成及代镠與綰戰，斬首百餘級，綰屯龍興寺。

translations.literal: Cheng Ji fought in Liu's stead against Kuo, beheaded more than a hundred, and Kuo encamped at Longxing Temple.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Ji fought Kuo in Liu's place, took more than a hundred heads, and Kuo withdrew to Longxing Temple.

sentences.zh: 镠微服逾城而入，遣馬綽、王榮、杜建徽等分屯諸門，使顧全武備東府，全武曰：「東府不足慮，可慮者淮南爾，綰急，必召淮兵至，患不細矣。

translations.literal: Liu in plain dress crossed the wall to enter, dispatched Ma Chuo, Wang Rong, Du Jianhui, and others to encamp separately at the various gates, and had Gu Quanwu prepare defenses for the Eastern Capital; Quanwu said: "The Eastern Capital is not worth worrying over—what is worrisome is Huainan alone; when Kuo grows desperate he is sure to summon Huainan troops, and the danger will not be small.
translations.idiomatic: Liu slipped in disguised as a commoner. He posted Ma Chuo, Wang Rong, and Du Jianhui at the various gates and ordered Gu Quanwu to secure the Eastern Capital. Quanwu said: "The Eastern Capital is no great concern—the real worry is Huainan. Once Kuo grows desperate he will call in troops from the Huai, and the trouble will be serious.

sentences.zh: 楊公大丈夫，今以難告，必能閔我。

translations.literal: Lord Yang is a true great man; if we now tell him of our distress, he will surely pity us.
translations.idiomatic: Lord Yang is a man of stature. If we confide our plight to him now, he will surely show us mercy.

sentences.zh: 」镠以為然。

translations.literal: " Liu thought this correct.
translations.idiomatic: " Qian Liu agreed.

sentences.zh: 全武曰：「獨行，事必不濟，請擇諸公子可行者。

translations.literal: Quanwu said: "Alone, the affair will certainly not succeed; please choose from among your sons one who can go.
translations.idiomatic: Quanwu said: "If one man goes alone the mission will fail. Choose whichever of your sons is fit to accompany me.

sentences.zh: 」镠曰：「吾嘗欲以元鳷婚楊氏。

translations.literal: " Liu said: "I have long wished to marry Yuanqiu to the Yang clan.
translations.idiomatic: " Liu replied: "I have long wished to marry Qian Yuanqiu into the Yang family.

sentences.zh: 」乃使隨全武如廣陵。

translations.literal: " He then had him follow Quanwu to Guangling.
translations.idiomatic: " He sent Yuanqiu to accompany Quanwu to Guangling.

sentences.zh: 綰果召田頵於宣州。

translations.literal: Kuo indeed summoned Tian Jun from Xuanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: As expected, Xu Kuo summoned Tian Jun from Xuanzhou.

sentences.zh: 全武等至廣陵，行密以女妻元鳷，亟召頵還。

translations.literal: Quanwu and the others reached Guangling; Xingmi gave his daughter in marriage to Yuanqiu and urgently summoned Jun back.
translations.idiomatic: When Quanwu and his party reached Guangling, Yang Xingmi gave his daughter to Qian Yuanqiu in marriage and urgently recalled Tian Jun.

sentences.zh: 頵取镠錢百萬，質镠子元瓘而歸。

translations.literal: Jun took one million of Liu's cash, took Liu's son Yuanguan as hostage, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Jun took a million strings of Qian Liu's silver, accepted Liu's son Qian Yuanguan as hostage, and marched home.

sentences.zh: 天祐元年，封镠吳王，镠建功臣堂，立碑紀功，列賓佐將校名氏於碑陰者五百人。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianyou, Liu was enfeoffed as King of Wu; Liu built the Hall of Meritorious Ministers, erected a stele recording achievements, and listed on the back the names of retainers, assistants, and officers—five hundred in all.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tianyou Qian Liu was enfeoffed as King of Wu. He built the Hall of Meritorious Ministers and raised a victory stele, inscribing on its reverse the names of five hundred advisers, staff officers, and commanders.

sentences.zh: 四年，升衣錦城為安國衣錦軍。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, Brocade-Robed City was elevated to the Anguo Brocade-Robed Army.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year Brocade-Robed City was upgraded to the Anguo Brocade-Robed Army command.

sentences.zh: 梁太祖即位，封镠吳越王兼淮南節度使。

translations.literal: When the Founding Emperor of Liang ascended the throne, Liu was enfeoffed as King of Wuyue with concurrent appointment as Military Commissioner of Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: When the Liang Founder took the throne, Qian Liu was enfeoffed as King of Wuyue and concurrently made Military Commissioner of Huainan.

sentences.zh: 客有勸镠拒梁命者，镠笑曰：「吾豈失為孫仲謀邪！

translations.literal: A guest advised Liu to reject the Liang appointment; Liu smiled and said: "Would I fall short of being a Sun Zhongmou!
translations.idiomatic: When a retainer urged him to defy the Liang investiture, Qian Liu laughed and said: "Am I less than Sun Zhongmou?

sentences.zh: 」遂受之。

translations.literal: " He then accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: " He accepted the appointment.

sentences.zh: 太祖嘗問吳越進奏吏曰：「錢镠平生有所好乎？

translations.literal: The Founder once asked a Wu-Yue memorial clerk: "In his lifetime, did Qian Liu have anything he favored?
translations.idiomatic: The Founder once asked a Wu-Yue memorial clerk: "Did Qian Liu have any special likes in life?

sentences.zh: 」吏曰：「好玉帶、名馬。

translations.literal: ”The clerk said: “He loves jade belts and famous horses.
translations.idiomatic: ”The clerk said, “Jade belts and fine horses—that is what he loves.”

sentences.zh: 」太祖笑曰：「真英雄也。

translations.literal: ”The Founder laughed and said: “A true hero.
translations.idiomatic: ”The Founder laughed. “Now that is a hero.”

sentences.zh: 」乃以玉帶一匣、打球御馬十匹賜之。

translations.literal: ”Thereupon he bestowed on him one case of jade belts and ten imperial polo horses.
translations.idiomatic: He then sent him a case of jade belts and ten imperial horses trained for polo.

sentences.zh: 江西危全諷等為楊渥所敗，信州危仔倡奔於镠，镠惡其姓，改曰元。

translations.literal: Wei Quanfeng and others in Jiangxi were defeated by Yang Wo; Wei Zichang of Xinzhou fled to Liu. Liu disliked his surname Wei and changed it to Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiangxi, Wei Quanfeng and his allies were routed by Yang Wo. Wei Zichang of Xinzhou fled to Qian Liu, who loathed the surname Wei and had it changed to Yuan.

sentences.zh: 開平二年，加镠守中書令，改臨安縣為安國縣，廣義鄉為衣錦鄉。

translations.literal: In the second year of Kaiping, Liu was promoted to Acting Director of the Secretariat; Lin'an County was renamed Anguo County, and Guangyi Township was renamed Yijin Township.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaiping 2, Qian Liu was made Acting Director of the Secretariat. Lin'an County became Anguo County, and Guangyi Township became Yijin Township.

sentences.zh: 三年，加守太保。

translations.literal: In the third year, he was further promoted to Acting Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was further promoted to Acting Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 楊渥將周本、陳章圍蘇州，镠遣其弟鋸、鏢救之。

translations.literal: Yang Wo's generals Zhou Ben and Chen Zhang besieged Suzhou; Liu sent his younger brothers Ju and Biao to the rescue.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Wo's generals Zhou Ben and Chen Zhang laid siege to Suzhou. Qian Liu sent his brothers Qian Ju and Qian Biao to relieve the city.

sentences.zh: 淮兵為水柵環城，以銅鈴系網沈水中，斷潛行者。

translations.literal: The Huai armies built water palisades around the city, hung copper bells from nets sunk in the water, and cut off anyone who tried to slip through underwater.
translations.idiomatic: The Huainan troops ringed the city with floating barriers, hung copper bells from submerged nets, and blocked anyone who tried to swim through unseen.

sentences.zh: 水軍卒司馬福，多智而善水行，乃先以巨竹觸網，淮人聞鈴聲遂舉網，福乃過，入城中，其出也亦然。

translations.literal: A naval soldier named Sima Fu, clever and skilled at moving through water, first struck the net with a huge bamboo pole; when the Huai men heard the bell they raised the net, and Fu passed through and entered the city; when he came out he did the same.
translations.idiomatic: The fleet private Sima Fu was shrewd and a master of the water. He would poke the net with a great bamboo pole first; when the Huainan men heard the bells they lifted the net, and Fu slipped through into the city—and left the same way.

sentences.zh: 乃取其軍號，內外夾攻，號令相應，淮人以為神，遂大敗之，本等走，擒其將閭丘直、何明等。

translations.literal: He then took their military signals; inside and outside attacked together, orders answering each other; the Huai men thought it supernatural, and were utterly defeated; Ben and the others fled; they captured their generals Luqiu Zhi, He Ming, and others.
translations.idiomatic: Then he seized their battle signals. Forces inside and out struck together, commands falling in perfect answer. The Huainan troops took it for sorcery and broke in rout. Ben and the rest fled; their generals Luqiu Zhi, He Ming, and others were captured.

sentences.zh: 四年，镠遊衣錦軍，作《還鄉歌》曰：「三節還鄉兮掛錦衣，父老遠來相追隨。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, Liu toured Yijin Army and composed the "Song of Returning Home," saying: "With three commissions homeward bound, brocade robes hung; the elders come from afar to follow in train.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year Qian Liu visited Yijin Army and wrote the "Song of Returning Home": "Homeward with my triple seal, brocade cloak swinging wide— / Elders from far and near trail after me."

sentences.zh: 牛鬥無孛人無欺，吳越一王駟馬歸。

translations.literal: No baleful star in the Dipper, no man deceives; one king of Wu-Yue, four horses returning.
translations.idiomatic: No ill omen hangs over the Ox Dipper; no man cheats another— / One king rules Wu and Yue; four matched horses bear him home."

sentences.zh: 」乾化元年，加镠守尚書令，兼淮南、宣潤等道四面行營都統。

translations.literal: ”In the first year of Qianhua, Liu was promoted to Acting Director of the Secretariat and made overall commander of the mobile camps on all four sides for the Huainan, Xuan, and Run circuits.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianhua 1 he was made Acting Director of the Secretariat and Overall Commander of the Mobile Camps on All Four Sides for Huainan, Xuan, Run, and related circuits.

sentences.zh: 立生祠於衣錦軍。

translations.literal: A living shrine was erected at Yijin Army.
translations.idiomatic: A living shrine was raised at Yijin Army.

sentences.zh: 镠弟鏢居湖州，擅殺戍將潘長，懼罪奔於淮南。

translations.literal: Liu's younger brother Biao held Huzhou; he killed the garrison commander Pan Chang on his own authority, feared punishment, and fled to Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Liu's brother Qian Biao was stationed at Huzhou. He killed the garrison commander Pan Chang on his own authority, feared retribution, and fled to Huainan.

sentences.zh: 二年，梁郢王友珪立，冊尊镠尚父。

translations.literal: In the second year, Liang Prince of E Yougui ascended the throne and ennobled Liu as Imperial Father.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year, when Liang's Prince of E, Yougui, took the throne, Qian Liu was ennobled as Imperial Father.

sentences.zh: 末帝貞明三年，加镠天下兵馬都元帥，開府置官屬。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhenming under the Last Emperor, Liu was promoted to overall commander of all armies and horses under heaven; he opened a headquarters and established an official staff.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenming 3 of the Last Emperor, Qian Liu was made Overall Commander of All Armies and Horses Under Heaven, opened a grand headquarters, and appointed a full staff.

sentences.zh: 四年，楊隆演取虔州，镠始由海路入貢京師。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, Yang Longyan took Qianzhou; Liu began to send tribute to the capital by sea.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year Yang Longyan took Qianzhou, and Qian Liu began sending tribute to the capital by sea.

sentences.zh: 龍德元年，賜镠詔書不名。

translations.literal: In the first year of Longde, Liu was granted the privilege of imperial rescripts without naming him.
translations.idiomatic: In Longde 1 Qian Liu was granted imperial rescripts that did not name him.

sentences.zh: 唐莊宗入洛，镠遣使貢獻，求玉冊。

translations.literal: When Tang Emperor Zhuangzong entered Luoyang, Liu sent envoys with tribute and requested a jade register.
translations.idiomatic: When Tang Emperor Zhuangzong entered Luoyang, Qian Liu sent envoys with tribute and asked for a jade register.

sentences.zh: 莊宗下其議於有司，群臣皆以謂非天子不得用玉冊，郭崇韜尤為不可，既而許之，乃賜镠玉冊金印。

translations.literal: Zhuangzong referred the matter to the responsible offices for deliberation; the court ministers all held that only the Son of Heaven might use a jade register; Guo Chongtao was especially opposed; yet in the end it was granted, and Liu was bestowed a jade register and gold seal.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuangzong referred the request to the ministries. The ministers held that only the Son of Heaven might use a jade register; Guo Chongtao was especially adamant against it. Even so, permission was granted, and Qian Liu received a jade register and gold seal.

sentences.zh: 镠因以鎮海等軍節度授其子元瓘，自稱吳越國王，更名所居曰宮殿、府曰朝，官屬皆稱臣，起玉冊、金券、詔書三樓於衣錦軍，遣使冊新羅、渤海王，海中諸國，皆封拜其君長。

translations.literal: Liu thereupon invested his son Yuanguan with the Zhenhai military commission and the like; styled himself King of Wu-Yue; renamed his residence "palace" and his office "court"; all his officials called themselves ministers; erected three towers at Yijin Army for the jade register, gold voucher, and imperial rescripts; sent envoys to invest the kings of Silla and Bohai; and for all the states across the sea, conferred titles on their rulers.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Liu then transferred the Zhenhai command and related posts to his son Qian Yuanguan, styled himself King of Wu-Yue, renamed his residence "Palace" and his headquarters "Court," and had all officials call themselves ministers. At Yijin Army he built three towers for the jade register, gold voucher, and imperial rescripts; sent envoys to invest the kings of Silla and Bohai; and for every state across the sea, conferred titles on their rulers.

sentences.zh: 元瓘字明寶，少為質於田頵。

translations.literal: Yuanguan, styled Mingbao, in his youth was sent as hostage to Tian Jun.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Yuanguan, styled Mingbao, spent his youth as a hostage with Tian Jun.

sentences.zh: 頵叛於吳，楊行密會越兵攻之，頵每戰敗歸，即欲殺元瓘，頵母嘗蔽護之。

translations.literal: When Jun rebelled against Wu, Yang Xingmi joined Yue troops to attack him; each time Jun returned defeated from battle he wanted to kill Yuanguan; Jun's mother often shielded him.
translations.idiomatic: When Jun rebelled against Wu, Yang Xingmi joined Wu-Yue troops in attacking him. Each time Jun came back defeated he meant to kill Yuanguan; Jun's mother repeatedly shielded him.

sentences.zh: 後頵將出，語左右曰：「今日不勝，必斬錢郎。

translations.literal: Later when Jun was about to go out to battle, he told those around him: "If I do not win today, I will certainly execute Lord Qian.
translations.idiomatic: Later, as Jun was about to take the field, he told his attendants, "If I do not win today, I will cut off Lord Qian's head."

sentences.zh: 」是日頵戰死，元瓘得歸。

translations.literal: ”That day Jun died in battle, and Yuanguan was able to return.
translations.idiomatic: That very day Jun fell in battle, and Yuanguan made it home.

sentences.zh: 镠臥病，召諸大將告之曰：「吾子皆愚懦，不足任後事，吾死，公等自擇之。

translations.literal: Liu lay ill; he summoned his great generals and told them: "My sons are all foolish and timid, not fit to manage what comes after; when I die, you yourselves choose among them.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Liu fell ill and summoned his chief generals. "My sons are all dull and timorous," he said, "unfit to carry what comes after. When I die, choose among them yourselves."

sentences.zh: 」諸將泣下，皆曰：「元瓘從王征伐最有功，諸子莫及，請立之。

translations.literal: ”The generals wept; all said: "Yuanguan followed the Prince in campaigns with the greatest merit; none of the sons can match him; we ask that he be enthroned.
translations.idiomatic: The generals wept. "Yuanguan followed the Prince on campaign and earned the greatest merit," they said. "None of the sons can match him. We ask that he succeed."

sentences.zh: 」镠乃出管鑰數篋，召元瓘與之曰：「諸將許爾矣。

translations.literal: ”Liu thereupon brought out several boxes of keys and seals, summoned Yuanguan and gave them to him, saying: "The generals have agreed to you.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Liu brought out several boxes of keys and seals, called Yuanguan forward, and handed them over. "The generals have chosen you," he said.

sentences.zh: 」镠卒，元瓘立，襲封吳越國王，玉冊、金印，皆如镠故事。

translations.literal: ”Liu died; Yuanguan succeeded; he inherited the enfeoffment as King of Wu-Yue; jade register and gold seal, all as in Liu's precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Liu died. Yuanguan succeeded, inherited the kingship of Wu-Yue, and received jade register and gold seal by the same precedent as his father.

sentences.zh: 王延政自立於建州，閩中大亂，元瓘遣其將仰詮、薛萬忠等攻之，逾年，大敗而歸。

translations.literal: Wang Yanzheng declared himself at Jianzhou; Min was in great turmoil; Yuanguan sent his generals Yang Quan, Xue Wanzhong, and others to attack him; after more than a year they suffered great defeat and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yanzheng declared himself at Jianzhou and threw Min into chaos. Yuanguan sent Yang Quan, Xue Wanzhong, and others against him; after more than a year they were badly beaten and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 元瓘亦善撫將士，好儒學，善為詩，使其國相沈崧置擇能院，選吳中文士錄用之。

translations.literal: Yuanguan also knew how to win over officers and men, loved Confucian learning, and was adept at poetry; he had his chief minister Shen Song establish the Selection of Talent Academy and chose Wu scholars for appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanguan also knew how to comfort his troops, loved the Confucian classics, and wrote poetry well. He had his chief minister Shen Song establish the Academy for Selecting Talent and recruited Wu literati for office.

sentences.zh: 然性尤奢僭，好治宮室。

translations.literal: Yet by nature he was especially extravagant and presumptuous, fond of building palaces.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was by nature extravagantly presumptuous and loved to build palaces.

sentences.zh: 天福六年，杭州大火，燒其宮室迨盡，元瓘避之，火輒隨發。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Tianfu, a great fire at Hangzhou burned his palaces almost entirely; Yuanguan fled from it, and the fire would flare up wherever he went.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianfu 6 a great fire at Hangzhou burned his palaces nearly to ash. Yuanguan fled, and wherever he went the flames followed.

sentences.zh: 元瓘大懼，因病狂。

translations.literal: Yuanguan was greatly afraid and went mad from illness.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanguan was terrified and lost his mind to illness.

sentences.zh: 是歲卒，年五十五，謚曰文穆。

translations.literal: That year he died, aged fifty-five; posthumous title Wenmu.
translations.idiomatic: He died that year at fifty-five. His posthumous title was Wenmu.

sentences.zh: 子佐立。

translations.literal: His son Zuo succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Qian Zuo succeeded.

sentences.zh: 佐字祐，立時年十三，諸將皆少佐，佐初優容之，諸將稍不法，佐乃黜其大將章德安於明州、李文慶於睦州，殺內都監杜昭達、統軍使闞璠，由是國中皆畏恐。

translations.literal: Zuo, styled You, was thirteen when he succeeded; the generals all looked down on Zuo as young; at first Zuo treated them indulgently; the generals gradually grew lawless; Zuo then removed his great general Zhang Dean to Mingzhou and Li Wenqing to Muzhou, killed Internal Overseer Du Zhaoda and Army Controller Kan Fan—and from this the realm was filled with fear.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Zuo, styled You, was thirteen when he took the throne. The generals looked down on his youth; at first he indulged them, and they slowly grew unruly. Zuo then banished Zhang Dean, his chief general, to Mingzhou, and Li Wenqing to Muzhou; he executed Internal Overseer Du Zhaoda and Army Controller Kan Fan. From then on the whole realm lived in fear.

sentences.zh: 王延義、延政兄弟相攻，卓儼明、朱文進、李仁達等自相篡殺，連兵不解者數年。

translations.literal: The brothers Wang Yanyi and Yanzheng fought each other; Zhuo Yanming, Zhu Wenjin, Li Renda, and others overthrew and killed one another in succession; armies were continuously engaged for several years.
translations.idiomatic: The brothers Wang Yanyi and Wang Yanzheng turned on each other; Zhuo Yanming, Zhu Wenjin, Li Renda, and others seized and slaughtered one another in turn. War dragged on for years without pause.

sentences.zh: 仁達附於李景，已而又叛，景兵攻之，仁達求救於佐。

translations.literal: Renda submitted to Li Jing, then rebelled again; Jing's army attacked him; Renda begged Zuo for rescue.
translations.idiomatic: Li Renda submitted to Li Jing, then rebelled again. When Jing's army attacked him, Renda begged Qian Zuo for aid.

sentences.zh: 佐召諸將計事，諸將皆不欲行，佐奮然曰：「吾為元帥，而不能舉兵邪？

translations.literal: Zuo summoned the generals to discuss the matter; none wished to go; Zuo stirred himself and said: "I am commander-in-chief—can I not raise troops?
translations.idiomatic: Zuo called his generals to council. None wanted to march. He flushed and said, "I am commander-in-chief—can I not raise an army?"

sentences.zh: 諸將吾家素畜養，獨不肯以身先我乎？

translations.literal: You generals my family has always kept and nurtured—will none of you alone lead the way before me?
translations.idiomatic: You generals my house has fed and kept all these years—will not one of you go before me?"

sentences.zh: 有異吾議者斬！

translations.literal: Whoever disagrees with me, behead him!
translations.idiomatic: Whoever opposes me—off with his head!"

sentences.zh: 」乃遣其統軍使張筠、趙承泰等率兵三萬，水陸赴之。

translations.literal: ”Thereupon he sent his army controller Zhang Yun, Zhao Chengtai, and others with thirty thousand troops, going by land and water to hurry to their aid.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Army Controller Zhang Yun, Zhao Chengtai, and others with thirty thousand men by land and water to their relief.

sentences.zh: 遣將誓軍，號令齊整。

translations.literal: He sent a general to swear in the army; orders and ranks were arrayed in good order.
translations.idiomatic: He dispatched a general to swear in the troops; commands rang out in tight order.

sentences.zh: 筠等大敗景兵，俘馘萬計，獲其將楊業、蔡遇等，遂取福州而還，由是諸將皆服。

translations.literal: Yun and the others utterly defeated Jing's army; captives and severed heads numbered in the tens of thousands; they took his generals Yang Ye, Cai Yu, and others; they then took Fuzhou and returned—and from this the generals all submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yun and the rest routed Li Jing's army. Captives and severed heads numbered in the tens of thousands; they took Jing's generals Yang Ye, Cai Yu, and others, seized Fuzhou, and returned. From that day the generals submitted in earnest.

sentences.zh: 佐立七年，襲封吳越國王，玉冊、金印，皆如元瓘。

translations.literal: Zuo had reigned seven years when he inherited enfeoffment as King of Wu-Yue; jade register and gold seal, all as with Yuanguan.
translations.idiomatic: After seven years on the throne Qian Zuo inherited the kingship of Wu-Yue and received jade register and gold seal by Yuanguan's precedent.

sentences.zh: 開運四年，佐卒，年二十，謚曰忠獻。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Kaiyun, Zuo died, aged twenty; posthumous title Zhongxian.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaiyun 4 Qian Zuo died at twenty. His posthumous title was Zhongxian.

sentences.zh: 弟俶立。

translations.literal: His younger brother Chu succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Qian Chu succeeded.

sentences.zh: 俶字文德。

translations.literal: Chu, styled Wende.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Chu, styled Wende.

sentences.zh: 佐卒，弟倧以次立。

translations.literal: When Zuo died, his younger brother Zong succeeded by order of succession.
translations.idiomatic: When Zuo died, his younger brother Qian Zong succeeded by order of birth.

sentences.zh: 初，元瓘質於宣州，以胡進思、戴惲等自隨，元瓘立，用進思等為大將。

translations.literal: Initially, when Yuanguan was hostage at Xuanzhou, Hu Jinsi, Dai Yun, and others accompanied him; when Yuanguan succeeded, he employed Jinsi and the others as great generals.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Yuanguan was a hostage at Xuanzhou, Hu Jinsi, Dai Yun, and others went with him. When Yuanguan took the throne he made Jinsi and the rest chief generals.

sentences.zh: 佐既年少，進思以舊將自待，甚見尊禮，及倧立，頗卑侮之，進思不能平。

translations.literal: Zuo being still young, Jinsi expected deference as an old general and was greatly honored; when Zong succeeded, he was rather slighted and insulted—Jinsi could not bear it.
translations.idiomatic: While Zuo was still young, Jinsi, as an old commander, expected respect and was treated with great honor. When Zong succeeded, he was openly slighted and insulted; Jinsi could not swallow the humiliation.

sentences.zh: 倧大閱兵於碧波亭，方第賞，進思前諫以賞太厚，倧怒擲筆水中曰：「以物與軍士，吾豈私之，何見咎也！

translations.literal: Zong reviewed troops on a grand scale at Bibo Pavilion; just as rewards were being ranked, Jinsi stepped forward and remonstrated that the rewards were too generous; Zong in anger flung his brush into the water and said: "I give goods to the soldiers—how can I be keeping them for myself? Why blame me!
translations.idiomatic: Zong held a grand review at Bibo Pavilion and was ranking rewards when Jinsi stepped forward and said the gifts were too lavish. Zong angrily threw his brush into the water. "I am giving things to the soldiers—do you think I am hoarding them? Why reproach me?"

sentences.zh: 」進思大懼。

translations.literal: ”Jinsi was greatly afraid.
translations.idiomatic: Jinsi was terrified.

sentences.zh: 歲除，畫工獻《鐘馗擊鬼圖》，倧以詩題圖上，進思見之大悟，知倧將殺己。

translations.literal: At year's end, a painter presented "Zhong Kui Beating Demons"; Zong inscribed a poem on the painting; Jinsi saw it and understood fully, knowing Zong intended to kill him.
translations.idiomatic: At year's end a painter presented "Zhong Kui Beating Demons." Zong inscribed a poem on the scroll. Jinsi read it, understood at once, and knew Zong meant to kill him.

sentences.zh: 是夕擁衛兵廢倧，囚於義和院，迎俶立之，遷倧於東府。

translations.literal: That night he gathered the guard, deposed Zong, and imprisoned him in Yihe Hall; they welcomed Chu and enthroned him; Zong was moved to the Eastern Residence.
translations.idiomatic: That night he rallied the guard, deposed Zong, and imprisoned him in Yihe Hall. They welcomed Chu and set him on the throne; Zong was moved to the Eastern Residence.

sentences.zh: 俶歷漢、周，襲封吳越國王，賜玉冊、金印。

translations.literal: Chu lived through Han and Zhou, inherited enfeoffment as King of Wu-Yue, and was granted jade register and gold seal.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Chu lived through the Han and Zhou dynasties, inherited the kingship of Wu-Yue, and received jade register and gold seal.

sentences.zh: 世宗征淮南，詔俶攻常、宣二州以牽李景，俶治國中兵以待。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizong campaigned against Huainan, he ordered Chu to attack Chang and Xuan prefectures to tie down Li Jing; Chu prepared the realm's troops and waited.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shizong marched on Huainan, he ordered Chu to strike Chang and Xuan prefectures to pin down Li Jing. Chu mustered the realm's forces and waited.

sentences.zh: 景聞周師將大舉，乃遣使安撫，境上皆戒嚴。

translations.literal: Jing heard the Zhou army was about to march in force; he sent envoys to mollify border regions; all along the frontier they went on alert.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jing heard the Zhou army was about to move in strength and sent envoys to soothe the borders. Every frontier post went on alert.

sentences.zh: 蘇州候吏陳滿不知景使，以謂朝廷已克諸州，遣使安撫矣，亟言於俶，請舉兵以應。

translations.literal: Chen Man, a frontier clerk at Suzhou, did not know Jing's envoys had come; thinking the court had already taken the prefectures and sent envoys to pacify the region, he urgently reported to Chu and asked that troops be raised in response.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Man, a border clerk at Suzhou, did not know Jing's envoys had arrived. He thought the court had already captured the prefectures and sent pacifying envoys, and urgently urged Chu to raise troops in response.

sentences.zh: 俶相國吳程遽調兵以出，相國元德昭以為王師必未渡淮，與程爭於俶前，不可奪。

translations.literal: Chu's chancellor Wu Cheng hurriedly mobilized and marched out; Vice Censor-in-Chief Yuan Dezhao held that the imperial army surely had not yet crossed the Huai, and disputed with Cheng before Chu—he could not be overborne.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor Wu Cheng hurriedly mobilized and marched out. Chancellor Yuan Dezhao argued before Chu that the imperial army surely had not yet crossed the Huai and disputed with Cheng, but could not prevail.

sentences.zh: 程等攻常州，果為景將柴克宏所敗，程裨將邵可遷力戰，可遷子死馬前，猶戰不顧，程等僅以身免。

translations.literal: Cheng and the others attacked Changzhou and were indeed defeated by Jing's general Chai Kehong; Cheng's lieutenant Shao Keqian fought hard; Keqian's son died before his horse yet he still fought without looking back; Cheng and the others barely escaped with their lives.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Cheng and the rest attacked Changzhou and were beaten by Li Jing's general Chai Kehong. Cheng's lieutenant Shao Keqian fought on fiercely; his son fell dead before his horse, yet he still would not turn back. Cheng and the others barely escaped with their lives.

sentences.zh: 周師渡淮，俶乃盡括國中丁民益兵，使邵可遷等以戰船四百艘、水軍萬七千人至於通州以會期。

translations.literal: When the Zhou army crossed the Huai, Chu then conscripted every able-bodied man in the realm to augment his forces and sent Shao Keqian and others with four hundred warships and seventeen thousand naval troops to Tongzhou to meet the appointed rendezvous.
translations.idiomatic: Once the Zhou army crossed the Huai, Chu conscripted every able-bodied man in the realm to swell his ranks and sent Shao Keqian and others with four hundred warships and seventeen thousand sailors to Tongzhou for the rendezvous.

sentences.zh: 吳越自唐末有國，而楊行密、李據有江淮。

translations.literal: Wu-Yue had had its realm since late Tang, while Yang Xingmi and Li Ju held the Jiang-Huai region.
translations.idiomatic: Wu-Yue had held its realm since late Tang, while Yang Xingmi and Li Ju controlled the Jiang-Huai.

sentences.zh: 吳越貢賦，朝廷遣使，皆由登、萊泛海，歲常飄溺其使。

translations.literal: Wu-Yue's tribute and taxes, when the court sent envoys, all went by sea via Deng and Lai—they regularly lost envoys to storms and drowning each year.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the court sent envoys for Wu-Yue's tribute, the route ran by sea through Deng and Lai—and year after year envoys were lost to wind and drowning.

sentences.zh: 顯德四年，詔遣左諫議大夫尹日就、吏部郎中崔頌等使於俶，世宗諭之曰：「朕此行決平江北，卿等還當陸來也。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Xiande, an edict dispatched Left Remonstrator Yin Riujiu, Ministry of Personnel bureau director Cui Song, and others as envoys to Chu; Emperor Shizong instructed them: "On this campaign I am determined to pacify the lands north of the river; when you return you should come by land.
translations.idiomatic: In Xiande 4 an edict sent Left Remonstrator Yin Riujiu, Ministry of Personnel Bureau Director Cui Song, and others as envoys to Chu. Emperor Shizong told them, "I mean to pacify the lands north of the river on this campaign. When you return, you will come by land."

sentences.zh: 」五年，王師征淮，正月克靜海軍，而日就等果陸還。

translations.literal: ”In the fifth year the imperial army campaigned against Huainan; in the first month Jinghai Army was taken—and Riujiu and the others indeed returned by land.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year the imperial army marched on Huainan. In the first month Jinghai Army fell—and Yin Riujiu and the rest did return by land.

sentences.zh: 世宗已平淮南，遣使賜俶兵甲旗幟、橐駝羊馬。

translations.literal: After Shizong had pacified Huainan, he sent envoys bestowing on Chu armor, flags and banners, camels, sheep, and horses.
translations.idiomatic: After Shizong pacified Huainan, he sent envoys bearing armor, flags and banners, camels, sheep, and horses as gifts to Chu.

sentences.zh: 錢氏兼有兩浙幾百年，其人比諸國號為怯弱，而俗喜淫侈，偷生工巧，自镠世常重斂其民以事奢僭，下至雞魚卵鷇，必家至而日取。

translations.literal: The Qian clan had held both Zhe circuits for nearly a century; their people compared with other states were called cowardly and weak, yet the customs favored indulgence and luxury, clinging to life and skilled in craft; from Liu's time they constantly levied heavily on the people to serve extravagance and presumption; down to chickens, fish, eggs, and nestlings—they had to visit every household and take daily.
translations.idiomatic: The Qian had ruled both Zhe circuits for nearly a hundred years. Neighboring states called their people timid and soft, yet the land loved luxury and excess, clinging to ease and clever in craft. From Qian Liu's day they taxed the people relentlessly to feed royal extravagance—down to chickens, fish, eggs, and nestlings, taken house by house, day by day.

sentences.zh: 每笞一人以責其負，則諸案史各持其簿列於廷；

translations.literal: Each time one man was flogged to punish his arrears, the clerks of every desk would hold their ledgers and line up in the hall;
translations.idiomatic: Whenever one man was beaten for debt, the clerks of every desk stood in the hall with their ledgers.

sentences.zh: 凡一簿所負，唱其多少，量為笞數，以次唱而笞之，少者猶積數十，多者至笞百餘，人尤不勝其苦。

translations.literal: For each ledger's arrears they would call out the amount and fix the number of strokes; they would beat them in order one by one; the lightest still accumulated dozens, the heaviest reached more than a hundred strokes—people could scarcely bear the suffering.
translations.idiomatic: For each ledger they called out what was owed and fixed the strokes accordingly, beating debtor after debtor in turn. Even the lightest cases piled up to dozens of blows; the heaviest ran to more than a hundred. The people could scarcely endure it.

sentences.zh: 又多掠得嶺海商賈寶貨。

translations.literal: They also plundered much treasure from merchants of the Lingnan coast and the sea routes.
translations.idiomatic: They also seized great store of merchant treasure from the southern coast and the sea lanes.

sentences.zh: 當五代時，常貢奉中國不絕。

translations.literal: During the Five Dynasties they constantly sent tribute to China without cease.
translations.idiomatic: Through the Five Dynasties they never ceased sending tribute to the central court.

sentences.zh: 及世宗平淮南，宋興，荊、楚諸國相次歸命，俶勢益孤，始傾其國以事貢獻。

translations.literal: When Shizong pacified Huainan and Song rose, Jing-Chu states submitted one after another; Chu's position grew more isolated; he began to pour out the realm in tribute.
translations.idiomatic: When Shizong pacified Huainan and the Song dynasty rose, the states of Jing and Chu submitted one after another. Chu grew ever more isolated and began to drain the realm for tribute.

sentences.zh: 太祖皇帝時，俶嘗來朝，厚禮遣還國，俶喜，益以器服珍奇為獻，不可勝數。

translations.literal: During Emperor Taizu's time, Chu once came to court; lavish courtesy and sent back to his realm; Chu rejoiced and increased gifts of vessels, robes, and rarities beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Taizu, Chu came to court once. The emperor treated him with great honor and sent him home. Chu rejoiced and redoubled his gifts of vessels, robes, and curios beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 太祖曰：「此吾帑中物爾，何用獻為！

translations.literal: Taizu said: "These are things from my treasury—what need to offer them!
translations.idiomatic: Taizu said, "These are already things in my treasury—why offer them at all?"

sentences.zh: 」太平興國三年，詔俶來朝，俶舉族歸於京師，國除。

translations.literal: ”In the third year of Taiping Xingguo, edict summoned Chu to court; Chu brought his whole clan to the capital; the state was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In Taiping Xingguo 3 an edict summoned Chu to court. He brought his whole clan to the capital, and the kingdom was abolished.

sentences.zh: 其後事具國史。

translations.literal: Subsequent events are detailed in the national histories.
translations.idiomatic: What followed is set out in the dynastic histories.

sentences.zh: 嗚呼！

translations.literal: Alas!
translations.idiomatic: Alas!

sentences.zh: 天人之際，為難言也。

translations.literal: The boundary between heaven and man is hard to speak of.
translations.idiomatic: Between heaven and man there are things hard to put into words.

sentences.zh: 非徒自古術者好奇而幸中，至於英豪草竊亦多自托於妖祥，豈其欺惑愚眾，有以用之歟？

translations.literal: Not only since antiquity have diviners been curious and lucky in hits—to heroes and bandits rising from the grass many also entrust themselves to omens and prodigies; was it to deceive the foolish masses that they had means to use them?
translations.idiomatic: It is not only that diviners since old times have been curious and lucky in their hits. Heroes and bandits rising from the wilds also often lean on omens and portents. Did they mean to beguile the foolish multitude—and find in that a tool they could use?

sentences.zh: 蓋其興也，非有功德漸積之勤，而黥髡盜販，倔起於王侯，而人亦樂為之傳歟？

translations.literal: Perhaps in their rise there was no gradual accumulation of merit and virtue, but tattooed criminals and shaved robber-traders suddenly standing among kings and marquises—and people also gladly spread their stories?
translations.idiomatic: Perhaps their rise held no slow accretion of merit, but tattooed outlaws and shaved robber-peddlers suddenly standing among kings and lords—and people were glad to tell their tales?

sentences.zh: 考錢氏之始終，非有德澤施其一方，百年之際，虐用其人甚矣，其動於氣象者，豈非其孽歟？

translations.literal: Examining the Qian clan from beginning to end—they did not shower one region with virtuous grace; across a century they cruelly used their people—was what moved in celestial signs not their retribution?
translations.idiomatic: Look at the Qian from first to last: they never showered one region with benevolent rule; across a century they cruelly used their people. Was what stirred in the heavens and earth not their retribution?

sentences.zh: 是時四海分裂，不勝其暴，又豈皆然歟？

translations.literal: At that time the four seas were split; unable to bear their tyranny—was it all thus everywhere?
translations.idiomatic: The four seas were torn apart then. Unable to bear such tyranny—was every land like this?

sentences.zh: 是皆無所得而推歟？

translations.literal: Is there nothing to be inferred from any of this?
translations.idiomatic: Can nothing at all be inferred from it?

sentences.zh: 術者之言，不中者多，而中者少，而人特喜道其中者歟？

translations.literal: Diviners' words mostly miss, few hit—and yet people especially love to tell of those that hit?
translations.idiomatic: Diviners' words mostly miss and rarely hit—yet people love above all to repeat the hits?

translations.literal: An opening editorial bracket marking the start of an explanatory note.
translations.idiomatic: [Editorial note:

sentences.zh: （镠世興滅，諸書皆同，蓋自唐乾寧二年為鎮海、鎮東軍節度使，兼有兩浙，至皇朝太平興國三年國除，凡八十四年。）〉

translations.literal: (The rise and fall of Liu's house--all books agree; from the second year of Qianning in Tang as military commissioner of Zhenhai and Zhendong, holding both Zhejiang circuits, until the third year of Taiping Xingguo in our dynasty when the state was abolished--in all eighty-four years.)
translations.idiomatic: (Accounts of Qian Liu's rise and fall agree across sources: from Tang Qianning 2 [895], when he became military commissioner of Zhenhai and Zhendong and held both Zhejiang provinces, until our dynasty's Taiping Xingguo 3 [978], when the kingdom was abolished--a total of eighty-four years.)
